ranked.headline: Sequence models link DNA motifs to chromatin accessibility, methylation and 3D folding
ranked.summary: Sequence-based deep models now predict accessibility, methylation and 3D contacts, with attribution and in silico perturbation dissecting drivers.

ranked.headline: Microbial sequence catalogues gain host and functional annotation at metagenomic scale
ranked.summary: Large metagenomic and genome resources now support prediction of functional elements, plasmid hosts, and prioritized variants from the same datasets.

ranked.headline: Computational methods denoise, impute and deconvolve single-cell transcriptomic data
ranked.summary: Deep learning and statistical frameworks now target dropout, cell identity, and deconvolution across scRNA-seq, chromatin, and FISH data.

ranked.headline: Generative protein design conditioned on sequence models, evolution and structure
ranked.summary: Recent work tests language-model generators under structural, evolutionary and signal-peptide constraints.

ranked.headline: Sequence-based models prioritize noncoding variants and regulatory elements
ranked.summary: Recent work extends variant and regulatory prioritization to RNA language models, long-read transcripts, and isoform-aware networks.

ranked.headline: Fused graph and fingerprint models dominate molecular activity and property prediction
ranked.summary: Recent items extend graph models to CNS penetration, activity cliffs, allergenicity, and debiased interaction benchmarks.

ranked.headline: Genomic and clinical data are combined to infer pathogen transmission and asymptomatic…
ranked.summary: Hospital transmission models and pooled-sequencing tools show genomic data supporting carrier inference and population-level lineage estimation.

ranked.headline: Modeling choices and data integration shape clinical outcome prediction performance
ranked.summary: Preprints and publications test how model form, risk-score fusion, subgroup discovery, and federated training change clinical prediction performance.

ranked.headline: Pretrained-embedding deep models predict RNA, protein and peptide binding sites
ranked.summary: Pretrained sequence embeddings are now paired with capsule, contrastive, and siamese objectives for site-level biomolecular prediction.

ranked.headline: Reference genome choice and haplotype-resolved assembly shape downstream genomic analysis
ranked.summary: Recent work shows reference quality, from near-complete assemblies to matched cell-line genomes, governs downstream variant and epigenomic analysis.

ranked.headline: Variant-aware deep learning spans INDEL mutation rates, splicing and rare-variant effects
ranked.summary: Recent preprints and publications apply genotype- and variant-aware neural models to mutation, splicing, and rare-variant prediction.

ranked.headline: Information theory and reproducible pipelines for omics, spatial, and phenotype data
ranked.summary: Recent open-source releases embed information-theoretic measures and end-to-end workflow packaging into omics and phenotype analysis tools.

ranked.headline: Aligning histology, spatial transcriptomics, and scRNA-seq across unpaired modalities
ranked.summary: Recent preprints align H&E tiles, spatial proteomics, and cell morphology with transcriptomic profiles without requiring paired measurements.

ranked.headline: Ensemble-based flexibility analysis across MD, BioEmu, and AlphaFold2 ensembles
ranked.summary: Flexibility is increasingly modeled as a conformational ensemble property, with new tools analyzing per-residue and dimensional variation across sampling…

ranked.headline: Spatial omics methods now link single-cell identity to tissue architecture
ranked.summary: Imaging platforms, H&E-based prediction, and spatially aware gene selection are being benchmarked and extended for single-cell tissue analysis.

ranked.headline: Graph-based models of brain connectivity across EEG, SEEG, fMRI and connectomes
ranked.summary: Recent preprints apply graph fusion and contrastive learning to EEG, SEEG, fMRI and structural connectomes for brain state and disease classification.

ranked.headline: Graph and foundation models infer transcriptional networks and perturbation responses
ranked.summary: Recent preprints and papers pair graph structure with single-cell foundation models to add spatial, knowledge and perturbation context to transcriptomic…

ranked.headline: Shrinkage and copula Bayesian models recover sparse markers from high-dimensional omics
ranked.summary: Sparse, interpretable estimators are being adapted to interaction, marker, and spatial-expression problems in high-dimensional omics data.

ranked.headline: Metabolic models resolve subject- and cell-level states from omics data
ranked.summary: Recent work applies flux-based inference, genome-scale reconstruction, and ME models to BRCA1 loss, Crohn's disease, and gut microbiome data.

ranked.headline: Benchmarked informatics workflows reshape proteomics analysis from DIA to proteogenomics
ranked.summary: Newly posted and published work evaluates DIA software, phasing methods, and pooled IP-MS, making method choice a central proteomics question.

ranked.headline: Scriptable tools for metagenomic simulation, sequence search, and motif discovery
ranked.summary: Recent tools target throughput and reproducibility for large microbial and metagenomic sequence datasets.

ranked.headline: Biological network structure guides candidate ranking and causal inference across omics
ranked.summary: Preprints now couple causal and graph-based network models to candidate ranking, from blood-test disease networks to single-cell perturbation effects.

ranked.headline: Models resolve binding paths, ensembles, and oligomers of disordered proteins
ranked.summary: Simulation frameworks now extend to disordered, phase-separating, and mixed folded-disordered targets, linking dynamics to binding and assembly.

ranked.headline: Learned protein representations drive interaction, affinity and structure prediction
ranked.summary: Sequence-only and graph-based models now predict binding affinity, host-pathogen interactions and interaction sites from pretrained embeddings.

ranked.headline: Software now fits and constrains mechanistic models of dynamic biological behavior
ranked.summary: Recent packages automate thermodynamic constraint, symbolic inference, and kinetic parameter fitting for dynamic biological models from noisy or multi-lab data.

ranked.headline: Computational methods probe TCR, antibody and peptide-MHC recognition specificity
ranked.summary: Paired-chain sequencing and benchmarked unsupervised TCR inference now test predictors against experimental and curated reference data.

ranked.headline: Static and bioelectric models of neuronal excitability and criticality
ranked.summary: Static maximum entropy and cross-species channel diversity analyses now probe what separates critical, excitable, and subcritical neural regimes.

ranked.headline: Single-cell data constrain dynamical models of gene regulation and cell fate
ranked.summary: Single-cell and spatiotemporal transcriptomics now constrain dynamic regulatory networks and virtual-cell simulations of cell state trajectories.

ranked.headline: Simulations of membrane geometry, fluctuations and cell motility across scales
ranked.summary: Recent preprints and a published study add shape-dependent migration, non-equilibrium membrane fluctuations and superdiffusive chemotaxis to membrane modeling.

ranked.headline: Protein language models and deep learning tools for genome interpretation
ranked.summary: Protein language model embeddings and deep learning gene predictors are becoming standardized, accessible tools for genome-scale annotation and viromics.

ranked.headline: MD sampling reveals allosteric networks underlying laccase and p53 Y220C regulation
ranked.summary: Recent simulations link allosteric pathways and conformational selection to ligand recognition, drug stabilization, and photoswitch activity.

ranked.headline: Evolutionary histories modeled as networks rather than bifurcating trees
ranked.summary: Recent preprints treat gene transfer, epistatic fitness landscapes, and strategy spaces as network-structured targets for inference and analysis.

ranked.headline: Structure-conditioned generative models for small molecules and peptides
ranked.summary: Recent preprints couple diffusion, flow-matching, and neural-field generators with pocket, target, and expert-feedback priors.

ranked.headline: Learning-rule models link synaptic plasticity to sparse coding and decision policy
ranked.summary: Explicit learning-rule models are now fit to neural and behavioral measures, tying plasticity mechanisms to coding and choice.

ranked.headline: Omitted epistasis distorts GWAS null statistics as QTL atlases widen scope
ranked.summary: Expanded molecular QTL and metabolite atlases raise discovery stakes just as preprint evidence shows omitted interactions can inflate GWAS test statistics.

ranked.headline: Demography and genome structure shape how lineage history is recorded across taxa
ranked.summary: Simulation-based Ks calibration, chromosome-level assemblies, and coupling estimates now quantify how genome features encode lineage history.

ranked.headline: Atlas registration and Bayesian models quantify regional brain cell counts
ranked.summary: Multimodal mouse brain datasets now align to common atlases, enabling quantitative comparison of cell density and anatomical geometry.

ranked.headline: Compressed inverted indexes and minimizer density models target scalable sequence search
ranked.summary: Onika targets collection-versus-collection similarity search, and minimizer density work refines the sketching layer beneath it.

ranked.headline: Software tools detect and visualize gene loss, recombination graphs and RNA pseudoknots
ranked.summary: Recent releases package detection and visualization of genomic and RNA structural features as usable command-line and interactive software.

ranked.headline: Generative design of peptide and ligand binders conditioned on target structure
ranked.summary: Flow-matching and chirality-agnostic algorithms now generate peptide sequences, all-atom structures, and D-peptide binders for protein targets.
